gen-fs-tanker-gf-julius-sans-one: Heavy and commanding, Tanker tucks its curves inward and packs its letters tight, while Julius Sans One spreads out with wide gaps. One feels shut, the other open.
gen-fs-tanker-gf-lexend-giga: Commanding and dense, Tanker curls its curves inward with barely a gap between letters. And Lexend Giga, a sans-serif with generous tracking, gives it room, while the heading earns its place when big and brief.
gen-fs-tanker-gf-lexend-peta: Heavy and commanding, Tanker curls every open curve inward and crowds its letters, while Lexend Peta, a sans-serif, gapes wide with big, unthinned curves. Shrink Tanker and that crowding turns muddy.
gen-fs-tanker-gf-lexend-tera: Dense, heavy slab of a headline: Tanker bends its curves inward and sits tight, while Lexend Tera spaces its open-faced sans letters like stepping stones. Shrink the heading, though, and that heft goes missing.
gen-fs-tanker-gf-montserrat-alternates: Montserrat Alternates reads wide open, its round letters matching their stems and its lowercase crowding toward the capital line, a sans-serif with chalk-board character. Tanker above it stays closed and heavy, and a whole page of the body would still feel light by comparison.
gen-fs-zina-fs-asap: Asap, a sans with open arcs and a body height nearly matching its capitals, sits beneath Zina's dramatic broad-nib swells. Fat strokes up top, quiet legibility below.
gen-fs-zina-fs-epilogue: Zina swings between fat downstrokes and threadlike upstrokes, a hairline gap running through it like cracked porcelain, over Epilogue's wire-like monoline sans. Its tall, curvy lowercase keeps a long page feeling easygoing.
gen-fs-zina-fs-merriweather-sans: Sharp, calligraphic drama up top. Zina's fat strokes and hairline thins sit above Merriweather Sans, a sans-serif whose tall lowercase and open e make words look sturdy and large.
gen-fs-zina-fs-supreme: Zina swings from stout stems to slim hairlines, striking and refined in a broad-nib way. But Supreme, a plain sans, holds a crisp, heavy-looking strip of text with letters kept open, which is where it does its best work.
gen-fs-zina-general-sans: General Sans reads like following a single thread, its x-height filling the line and every bend left unobstructed. And Zina above it swings from thick strokes to hair-thin ones, which is the pair's whole appeal.
